repose

/ri-POHZ/ — stress on second syllable, rhymes with 'suppose' · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Repose is a state of rest and peaceful calm, free from activity or stress.

After the harvest, the farmhands enjoyed a well-earned day of repose.

Example

After weeks of intense competition, the athlete finally found repose in a quiet resort, free from pressure and expectation.

Repose is more precise than 'rest' or 'sleep' because it specifically emphasizes peaceful calm and freedom from stress—not just physical recovery. You can rest anxiously; you cannot have repose without peace.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

rest: Rest is any break from work or effort — a nap, a weekend, five minutes on a bench — and it can be tense or fitful. Repose is rest of a deeper kind: settled, peaceful calm with the stress drained away. You can rest anxiously; repose is always serene.

relaxation: Relaxation is the process of loosening up — muscles unclenching, worries easing as you unwind. It points at the letting-go itself. Repose is the still state you arrive at afterward: complete, peaceful rest with no unwinding left to do. Relaxation is the road; repose is the destination.

respite: A respite is a short relief from something difficult — a pause in the storm, with more of it still to come. It is measured against the hardship around it. Repose is not squeezed between troubles: it is a settled state of peace and rest, free from strain on every side.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

turmoil: a state of great disturbance and confusion

commotion: noisy, disturbed, and busy activity

Where it sits · how peaceful and content you feel — agitation → weariness → repose → bliss

agitation vs. repose: Agitation is the opposite of repose: agitation is churning, restless disturbance, while repose is complete, peaceful rest.

weariness vs. repose: Weariness falls short of repose — weariness is the heavy tiredness that calls out for rest, while repose is the calm, restful state itself.

bliss vs. repose: Bliss goes beyond repose: repose is quiet, contented rest, while bliss rises all the way to perfect, overflowing happiness.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back; here it strengthens the meaning (Latin)

Root — pos(e)

Root — pos(e): to stop, to rest (as in pause) (Late Latin (pausare), from Greek (pausis, 'a stopping'))

Put it together

Put it together: re- ('back,' used here to strengthen the idea) + a root meaning 'to stop or pause' add up to 'settle back into stillness.' Repose is the deep, peaceful rest that comes when all activity stops.

Use the root in a new word: pause

Use the root in a new word: pause: Midway through practice, the coach called a pause before starting the next drill.

Word Choice

formal / literary

Repose is the word for profound, peaceful rest—not just physical recovery but true peace of mind. Reach for it when describing deep restoration and calm, especially in reflective or literary moments. For temporary breaks, 'respite' is lighter; for simple recovery from tiredness, 'rest' is plainer.
